title: Good arm day Vs Bad arm day
summary: First episode of a good-vs-bad day series, comparing a pump-chasing, high-rep, long-rest bro arm day with an intense arm day built on low exercise selection, RPE work, strict form, compounds and supersets. The description gives both templates and an empty skeleton to fill in.
claims: A bad arm day: 3x25 dumbbell curls, 3x20 triceps extensions, 3x20 spider curls, 3x20 kickbacks and 3x30 cable curls with 3 min rest between sets gives a pump and no gains, and takes forever

A good arm day: 3x6-10 close-grip bench + 3x3-5 weighted chin-ups; 3x6-10 dumbbell curls + 3x8-12 skull crushers or triceps extensions + 3x10-15 calf raises; 4x8-12 lateral raises or pin presses + 4x10-15 wrist curls + 4xAMRAP knee raises

Skeleton arm day: press or heavy arm movement 3x6-10 or 3x5 + pull 3x5 or 3x6-12; curl or triceps 3x6-10 + the other 3x8-12 + abs/calves 3x10-15; raises or press variation 4x8-12 + wrist flexion 4x10-15 + abs/calves 4xAMRAP; never two biceps or two triceps movements back to back, no extra presses if you opened with one
An arm day is one of the last steps of arm training; novices and often intermediates do not need one, but maximizing arm size eventually requires it
The idea that arms must be trained with high volume for the pump is a harmful myth
The pump is a poor measure of hypertrophy: metabolic fatigue, not the muscle, limits you, which removes muscle fiber damage and intensity
Train arms intensely: weights in the 3-7 or 6-10 rep range, or push to failure, not heavy swinging
You would never grow legs with sets of 30 at 135 lb on the squat; the same logic applies to biceps
A bad bro-split arm day stays bad when moved into a push/pull/legs program
Bro-split arm days use cables and machines at very high reps with many exercises; that is cardio for the arms and will not grow them
People with low biceps work capacity fool themselves by spending long hours on many curl variations
If arms are a weak point they tire easily: do three sets and move on, and only go to 7-8 sets once they can handle it
He does 5-6 sets of heavy biceps movements on his arm day, even while sandbagging biceps
Start with one exercise each for triceps, biceps and forearms, 3-4 sets each, and progress it like a bench or squat
Arm programs of 21-30 sets are pointless; cut them by 80 percent for better gains in less time
Pro bodybuilders and lying PED users train arms with huge volume and grow because of drugs; naturals cannot copy that
A good arm day works within intensity windows: RPE, set references, low set and exercise selection, milking each exercise before adding reps, sets or exercises
Arm progression is slow because they are small muscles; use microplates, as little as 2 lb jumps
Progressive overload works for biceps, just slower; it fails only when you chase the pump with 30-rep sets
The more exercises in a day, the harder progression becomes; focus on one
First-time arm days should use no cheat reps and a conservative range of motion
Locking out the elbow on biceps or triceps work adds no gains; it is fine if pain-free, but it is more likely to hurt the biceps tendon than grow the biceps
Train arms once a week to start; a good arm day is low-impact and can replace a rest day, sit between two lower-body days, or share the day with GPP
Do not put an arm day between two upper days unless it is programmed precisely for that; the triceps and biceps work can hurt pressing
Curls and skull crushers are isolation lifts; moving the shoulders in a curl turns it into a supinated clean, and moving them in a skull crusher offloads the triceps
An arm day is a good place for bench, horizontal press or vertical press variations, because it is not taxing and everything can be supersetted
An arm day without supersets is wasted time; while the biceps rest, train forearms, triceps, calves, abs, neck or GPP
The arm day should be the shortest, most compact day of the week, ideal for a weekend or low-energy day so energy is saved for squat and deadlift days
